text: Matchday XI · player cards · fairer tickets · transparent escrow

Introduce CricketVerse as a course prototype that connects matchday fantasy, player collectibles and ticketing. Live provider access depends on an API key and the provider feed; the default blockchain demo uses a local Hardhat chain.
The fan experience is split across systems
The match is shared. Ownership and trust are not.
Player cards and fan rewards stay locked inside platform databases.
Scoring and settlement can be difficult for fans to verify.
Resale can add markups while leaving organisers out of the loop.
Wallet setup and unreliable venue connectivity create friction.
Motivation: give fans assets they can own and rules they can verify.
Frame these as design problems addressed by the prototype, not claims about every cricket platform.
Use the chain where fans need shared proof
Keep fast-changing match data off-chain; put ownership and enforceable rules on-chain.

The blockchain adds value by making asset ownership portable and transaction rules independently checkable.
Motivation: use a public ledger for shared ownership and rules, not as a replacement for the match-data API. The current demo uses local Hardhat; no public deployment is configured.
APIs serve match data; contracts secure assets
A wallet separately signs each local-chain action.
Provider access needs a configured key and network connection. Contract demos default to a local chain.

Source basis: server/server.js and public/app.js implement provider-backed fixtures, playing XI and match points. BLOCKCHAIN_SETUP.md says the default chain is local Hardhat; the contracts are separate from the live sports API.
The API supplies the player pool; a squad hash links your picks to the on-chain contest entry.
At least 1 keeper · 3 batters · 3 bowlers · 1 all-rounder
A 120-credit cap and role minimums shape the squad. The live points feed remains an API input.

Source basis: /api/matches/today and /api/match/:id/playingXI in server/server.js; server/scoringEngine.js requires exactly 11 players, caps the squad at 120 credits, and enforces role minimums. BLOCKCHAIN_SETUP.md states contest entries commit a squad hash.
Fantasy points refresh from match data
The app reads provider points by player and updates the squad view.
While the match endpoint is reachable
A missing key, provider outage or incomplete feed stops live updates; cached/demo data is not presented as a live score.

Source basis: /api/match/:id/points aggregates provider batting, bowling and catching point fields. public/app.js polls the endpoint every 30 seconds. Provider API access requires CRICKET_API_KEY and a successful provider response.
ERC-1155 cards put player assets in fan wallets
Player data starts in the catalogue; ownership and rarity are tracked by the contract.
A card must be registered on the chain before it can be bought; stats require an authorised updater.

Source basis: server/data/players_2000_2026.json, BLOCKCHAIN_SETUP.md, and contracts/PlayerCardNFT.sol. The catalogue is server data; a card must be registered on the deployed chain before its primary sale can complete.
CRIC moves value through on-chain fan features
The demo token is used for primary card purchases, marketplace trades and contest entries.
Buy a card · trade an asset · join an escrow contest
Local test token only · CRIC has no public-chain deployment or real-world cash value in this demo.
Source basis: contracts/CRIC.sol and BLOCKCHAIN_SETUP.md. Local Hardhat demo uses the 50,000 CRIC faucet and a one-hour cooldown. Do not describe CRIC as a public or cash-equivalent asset.
Eight contracts put product rules on-chain
The code governs tokens, cards, tickets, trades, polls and contest funds.
The stats relay is not connected to a live Chainlink Functions subscription.
Source basis: eight Solidity files in contracts/. BLOCKCHAIN_SETUP.md identifies CricketOracleConsumer as an authorized relay and states a live Chainlink Functions subscription is not configured.
The ticket contract blocks resale above 115%
A check in the ERC-721 contract makes the resale ceiling enforceable by code.
A listing above this ceiling reverts, even if the app accepts the request.
The ticket cannot be used twice.
Source basis: contracts/MatchTicketNFT.sol and BLOCKCHAIN_SETUP.md. The contract enforces a 15% maximum markup and one-time redemption in the local demo.
The contract controls deposits and refunds; an organiser still settles winners.
Funds stay in contract escrow until settlement. Cancelled contests allow full refunds.

Source basis: contracts/TournamentPool.sol and BLOCKCHAIN_SETUP.md. Entry funds are held in escrow; the organiser locks the contest and submits winners. Refunds are available when the contest is cancelled.
Make fan trust easier to verify
These are outcomes to measure as the prototype is exercised, not results claimed today.
Measure card transfers and wallet-held assets.
Confirm over-cap listings revert in the contract.
Inspect deposits, payouts and refund events.
Measure offline checks and successful later sync.
These are expected impacts and proposed evaluation measures. No adoption, cost savings, anti-fraud rate or venue throughput improvement has been measured.
A credible local demo, with clear next steps
The blockchain features work in a local environment; public and oracle setup remain future work.

Blockchain tracks assets and enforces rules; the match feed supplies live cricket data.

Current scope is a course prototype on local Hardhat. The cricket provider adapter requires CRICKET_API_KEY and feed coverage. No public deployment, live Chainlink Functions subscription or trusted automatic tournament settlement is configured.
